memory_topology.how: DERIVED: nvidia-smi names the card 'NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090'. NVIDIA's shared-memory parts are the Tegra/Jetson line and GB10, all matched above this; a GeForce, Quadro, Tesla, TITAN or datacenter part has its own board memory behind a PCIe link.

backend.how: MEASURED: bin/llama.cpp/INSTALL.json, written by the setup script that installed this build

install_json.server_version: version: 0.3.0-dev (build 1, commit a32af33) built with GNU 15.2.0 for Linux x86_64

host_ram_gb.how: MEASURED: gpu_lock._memory_status() (GlobalMemoryStatusEx on Windows, /proc/meminfo on Linux)
host_ram_gb.note: total physical RAM as the OS reports it -- the same number gpu_lock sizes its per-job commit cap from

host_reserve_mib.how: MEASURED: MemTotal minus MemAvailable, 8 samples 1.0s apart
host_reserve_mib.desktop_state: live GNOME desktop: gnome-shell + Xwayland + Steam + browser, monitors on, recorded as-is by operator choice
host_reserve_mib.warning: min/max span this sample window ONLY, on whatever this box was doing at the time. On a unified or CPU-only box this is the anti-spill fence rule 14 is about, and it has to be measured under the load the campaign will actually run beside -- a reserve sampled on an idle box is a fence that moves when someone opens a browser.

igpu_share_limit_mib.why: not applicable: memory_topology is 'discrete', and only an integrated GPU has a driver-imposed share of system RAM

spec_bandwidth_gbs.why: no published bandwidth on file for 'NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090', and this script measures none. Pass --spec-bandwidth-gbs N --bandwidth-source '...' if rule 10's decode estimate is going to be published for this box.

cuda_arch.how: MEASURED: bin/llama.cpp/INSTALL.json, written by the setup script that built this llama.cpp

compute_cap.how: MEASURED: nvidia-smi --query-gpu=compute_cap -- the SM version this card actually is, which is what -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES has to match

ram_channels.how: DERIVED: 2 distinct (controller, channel) pairs among 2 populated DIMMs, from their SMBIOS type-17 locator strings

pl_writable_without_elevation.why: this process is running elevated (root/Administrator), and a successful set under elevation says nothing about the unelevated case. Re-run without elevation to answer it.

sudo_nopasswd.why: not asked. This process is already root, so `sudo -n true` would return 0 for that reason alone and would say nothing about the unelevated case - the same reason detect-machine.py:pl_write_test() refuses to run the power-limit write test under elevation.

privilege_path.how: DERIVED: elevated is true, so a privileged command runs in this process with no sudo in front of it

desktop_reserve_mib.how: MEASURED: nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used, 8 samples 1.0s apart with no llama.cpp process live
desktop_reserve_mib.desktop_state: live GNOME desktop: gnome-shell + Xwayland + Steam + browser, monitors on, recorded as-is by operator choice
desktop_reserve_mib.warning: min/max span this sample window ONLY. The reserve is what the desktop is DOING: the reference rig read 1,181 MiB idle and 1,669 MiB under a real workload, and shipped the worst case plus its load-to-load variation. Re-run with the desktop loaded before trusting max as an anti-spill fence (rule 14).
